# Dimension 6 — Coexistence

Running Claude Code and Codex on the same repository. Source details in
[citations](../citations.md).

## The instruction-file question, answered by both vendors

**Codex reads `AGENTS.md`.** Its discovery algorithm is documented in full [5]
and summarised in [setup-and-installation](setup-and-installation.md).

**Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, and says so explicitly:**

> "Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`. If your repository already
> uses AGENTS.md for other coding agents, create a CLAUDE.md that imports it so
> both tools read the same instructions without duplicating them. You can also
> add Claude-specific instructions below the import. Claude loads the imported
> file at session start, then appends the rest:" [54]

```markdown
@AGENTS.md

## Claude Code
Use plan mode for changes under `src/billing/`.
```

> "A symlink also works if you don't need to add Claude-specific content:
> `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md`… On Windows, creating a symlink requires
> Administrator privileges or Developer Mode, so use the `@AGENTS.md` import
> instead." [54]

Verification step Anthropic gives: run `/context` and confirm `CLAUDE.md`
appears under "Memory files" [54].

**Does Codex read `CLAUDE.md`?** No fetched OpenAI page mentions `CLAUDE.md`
anywhere — not the AGENTS.md guide [5], not the config reference [1]. But a
mechanism exists that would accept it:

> "If your repository already uses a different filename (for example
> `TEAM_GUIDE.md`), add it to the fallback list so Codex treats it like an
> instructions file." [5]

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
project_doc_fallback_filenames = ["TEAM_GUIDE.md", ".agents.md"]
```

Putting `"CLAUDE.md"` in that list is **mechanically within the documented shape
of the setting**, but no page states it, demonstrates it, or confirms it works.
Treat it as an untested inference, not documented behaviour.

**Recommended direction: `AGENTS.md` canonical, `CLAUDE.md` importing it.**
That is the pattern Anthropic itself documents [54], it is the only one that
works unchanged on Windows [54], and it lets Claude-specific content live below
the import rather than in a second maintained file.

## Four documented patterns, and when each breaks

| Pattern | Source | Breaks when |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` plus Claude-specific sections | [54] | Nothing found; the safest default |
| `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` | [54] | Windows without Administrator or Developer Mode [54]; a generator owns one of the files [65] |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` + `/init`, or `/import` — a one-time copy | [54] | Immediately: it is a snapshot that then drifts |
| `project_doc_fallback_filenames` on the Codex side | [5] | Untested with `CLAUDE.md`; also cannot be set at project scope alongside provider keys |

**The one non-obvious failure mode**, reported by a practitioner and not covered
by either vendor [65]:

> "If I symlinked them, one of two bad things would happen: Boost's regeneration
> would clobber my hand-written rules, or my edits would drift into a file a
> tool believes it owns. So the rule I actually follow is: symlink when both
> filenames are human-owned, keep them separate when a generator owns one, and
> put a line in the hand-written file telling agents the other exists." [65]

That is a Tier 3 practitioner report about a Laravel Boost-generated
`AGENTS.md`, labelled as such. The general shape — a framework or MCP server
that *writes* `AGENTS.md` and regenerates it on package update — is worth
checking for before symlinking anything.

## A size trap neither vendor documents

Codex truncates: it "stops adding files once the combined size reaches the limit
defined by `project_doc_max_bytes` (32 KiB by default)" [5]. Claude Code does
not: its files "are loaded in full regardless of length", with guidance to
"target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file" [54].

**A shared instruction set large enough for Claude Code can be silently
truncated by Codex.** Both facts are documented; the interaction between them is
an inference from the two pages, not stated anywhere. The lever is
`project_doc_max_bytes = 65536` [5]. (Whether the cap is per-file or combined is
itself unresolved — see
[setup-and-installation](setup-and-installation.md).)

## Precedence — similar shape, different mechanics

| | Claude Code [54] | Codex [5] |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | walk up the tree from CWD | walk **down** from project root to CWD |
| Combination | all discovered files concatenated, root-down | concatenated root-down, **at most one file per directory** |
| Scopes | managed policy → user → project → local (`CLAUDE.local.md`) | global `CODEX_HOME` → project chain |
| Override file | — | `AGENTS.override.md` suppresses the sibling `AGENTS.md` |
| Caching | — | "Codex rebuilds the instruction chain on every run… so there is no cache to clear manually" |
| Imports | `@path/to/import`, max four hops | not documented |
| Exclusions | `claudeMdExcludes` glob list | not documented |

The at-most-one-file-per-directory rule is the significant asymmetry: a
directory holding both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` gives Claude Code both (if
discovered) and Codex only one.

## MCP configuration does not port

| | Claude Code [53] | Codex [1][13] |
|---|---|---|
| User scope | `~/.claude.json` | `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| Project scope | `.mcp.json` | `.codex/config.toml` (trusted projects only) |
| Managed | `managed-mcp.json` | `requirements.toml` `mcp_servers` allowlist |
| Format | JSON | TOML |
| Precedence | "local > project > user" [55] | closest project file wins, then profile, user, system [2] |
| Trust model | workspace trust | `projects.<path>.trust_level` in the **global** file [1] |

**No vendor page claims the formats are interchangeable and none provides a
converter.** The only explicit statement that they are not is a practitioner
one: "Claude Code uses JSON; Codex uses TOML. You cannot paste one into the
other" [65]. The vendor docs corroborate the format difference without making
the claim.

Tool naming *is* shared: both use `mcp__<server>__<tool>` [10][52]. So MCP
*servers* port trivially in substance and awkwardly in syntax — a config
rewrite, not a redesign. What does not port is Claude Code's `Elicitation` and
`ElicitationResult` hook events for MCP user-input requests [52], which have no
entry in Codex's 11-event list [10].

There is one documented automated bridge, in one direction: Claude Code's
`/import` "carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents, and skills" from "a
supported coding agent's configuration" (v2.1.213+) [54]. **The page never
enumerates which agents are supported**, so whether it reads
`~/.codex/config.toml` is unestablished. The reverse — Codex's `/import` from
Claude Code [9] — defers to a page that returned 404 [68].

## Skills: the one thing that genuinely shares a home

Both implement the agentskills.io standard [21], and Codex's load paths include
`$HOME/.agents/skills` and `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills` [21] — a
vendor-neutral directory. Claude Code's are `~/.claude/skills/` and
`.claude/skills/` [53].

A practitioner reports keeping the canonical copies in `~/.agents/skills/` and
symlinking from `~/.claude/skills/`, with "most skills written for Claude Code
drop into Codex with zero edits", the exception being skills that name
Claude-specific tools — "Codex has shell access but no tool called Glob" [65].
Tier 3, self-reported, but consistent with both vendors' documented directory
layouts.

## Concurrent operation on one working tree

**Neither vendor documents it at all.** No fetched Anthropic or OpenAI page
discusses running a second agent on the same repository — not file locking, not
checkpointing, not sandbox writable roots interacting with another agent's
edits. That silence is itself the finding.

The only report found [65], Tier 3:

> "They coordinate through the filesystem, not through each other, so two agents
> editing the same file in the same minute will stale-read. Run them on
> different files, or hand off explicitly. Git is the arbiter of truth." [65]

The same source notes that context does not transfer — "A shared instructions
file gives both agents the same project knowledge, but not the same conversation
state" — and that Claude Code subagents "auto-dispatch" while "Codex expects you
to invoke things explicitly", so auto-routing orchestration "does not port"
[65]. That last point is consistent with OpenAI's own documentation:
"Current local Codex releases delegate when you ask directly or when applicable
AGENTS.md or skill instructions request it" [11].

And the blunt one, also [65]: **"Do I pay twice? Yes."** Coexistence means two
subscriptions or a subscription plus API spend.

For an `openshell-sandbox` user there is a cleaner isolation primitive than
either vendor discusses: **run the two agents in separate sandboxes.** Each gets
its own network policy, its own credential set, and its own copy of the repo,
which removes the concurrent-edit problem entirely at the cost of a manual
merge. That is an inference from the local tooling, not a cited claim.

## The AGENTS.md standard itself

> "A simple, open format for guiding coding agents, used by **over 60k
> open-source projects**." [62]

That number is a live GitHub code-search count for
`path:AGENTS.md NOT is:fork NOT is:archived`, undated on the page and not
independently verified here. It counts repositories containing a file at that
path, not projects using it meaningfully.

> "AGENTS.md is now stewarded by the **Agentic AI Foundation** (https://aaif.io)
> under the Linux Foundation." [62]

Origin: "collaborative efforts across the AI software development ecosystem,
including OpenAI Codex, Amp, Jules from Google, Cursor, and Factory" [62]. Repo
metadata: 23.8k stars, 1.8k forks, MIT licence [63].

**Claude Code does not appear on the spec site's compatible-agents list** — 23
tools are named including Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Zed, Windsurf and
Devin, and Claude Code is not among them [62]. A "View all supported agents"
link exists whose target was not captured, so this is not conclusive. It is a
curious gap given that Anthropic documents an AGENTS.md interop path on its own
site [54].

## Gaps and limitations

1. **The second practitioner source on coexistence was unreadable** — a
   JS-rendered page returning 0 chars [67]. Every conflict report in this file
   therefore rests on a single Tier 3 source [65] with a commercial interest in
   the topic.
2. Whether adding `"CLAUDE.md"` to `project_doc_fallback_filenames` actually
   works is an untested inference [5].
3. If `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md` **and** Codex is configured to
   read `CLAUDE.md` as a fallback, whether Codex double-loads is unaddressed;
   "at most one file per directory" [5] suggests not, but symlink resolution is
   never discussed.
4. Whether Claude Code's `/import` supports Codex specifically is unestablished
   [54]; Codex's `/import` artifact list is behind a 404 [68].
5. No jointly safe instruction-file size is stated by either vendor.
6. Concurrent operation on one working tree is undocumented by both vendors.
7. The 60k adoption figure is undated and unverified [62].
8. Why Claude Code is absent from the agents.md compatible list is unaddressed
   by any source.
